passages.note: Clere is recorded voting Nay on SB 101's House third reading (final passage).

passages.provision_quote: (b) A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: This is the compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means exemption test that SB 101 would have enacted; Clere voted against its final passage.

rows.reasoning: Clere voted Nay on SB 101 (2015), a single-subject bill creating a RFRA-style compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means exemption that matches rung 4 ('allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs'). His No vote shows opposition to that broad exemption but, under V4.2's rule that ruling out one rung is not evidence for which of the remaining rungs applies, does not by itself establish whether he holds rung 1, 2, or 3.
needs_source: Clere's own explanation of his Nay vote on SB 101 (2015) — a floor statement or contemporaneous own-words source — to establish which of rungs 1-3 he holds.
